name: Dow FRC Team Grant
description: General operating support for US and Canada FRC teams with a Dow employee mentor or located in a Dow community.
details: Submit through Dow's Submittable portal; you'll need your FIRST team number, a brief needs statement, and (if not in a Dow community) contact info for your Dow employee mentor. This cycle has closed — the next window typically opens in spring.

name: Dow FLL & FTC Team Grant
description: General operating support for US and Canada FLL and FTC teams with a Dow employee mentor or located in a Dow community.
details: Same Submittable process as the FRC grant: team number, needs statement, and Dow mentor/community documentation. This cycle has closed — check back in spring for the next application window.

name: BAE Systems FLL & FTC Team Grant
description: Funding for FLL and FTC teams, prioritizing those within 75 miles of a BAE Systems site, with a BAE mentor, at Title I schools, or in high-need communities.
amount: Varies; priority for Title I schools & high-need communities
details: Applied through BAE's Benevity grant form (linked from bae.firstrobotics@baesystems.com's official page). Priority goes to teams within 75 miles of a BAE site, with a BAE mentor, or at Title I schools — include that context in your application.

name: Digital Citizen Fund Rookie Team Grant
description: Sponsors participation of US-based rookie FRC teams with all or majority-female membership; up to five $5,000 grants awarded across two seasons.
details: Requires proof of rookie status and team roster showing all-female or majority-female membership. Only five grants are awarded across both seasons combined, so apply as early in the window as possible.

name: Fikret Yüksel Foundation Grant
description: Supports FRC teams competing in Türkiye regionals; requires a business plan, gender-equality action plan, and alumni engagement documentation.
details: Application (via Google Form, in Turkish) requires a written business plan, a gender-equality action plan, and documentation of how the team engages its alumni network — this is more paperwork-heavy than most US grants.

name: Arconic Foundation Grant
description: For rookie and veteran FLL, FTC, and FRC teams located in specific Arconic Foundation communities.
details: Only open to teams physically located in one of Arconic's listed plant communities — check the list on the Submittable page before starting an application, since being in the right state isn't enough on its own.

name: BAE Systems FRC Team Grant
description: Funding for FRC teams, prioritizing those within 75 miles of a BAE Systems site, with a BAE mentor, at Title I schools, or in high-need communities.
amount: Varies; priority for Title I schools & high-need communities
details: Applied through BAE's Benevity grant form. Priority goes to teams within 75 miles of a BAE site, with a BAE mentor, or at Title I schools/high-need communities — mention whichever applies to your team early in the form.

name: John Deere FIRST Team Grant
description: For FLL, FTC, and FRC teams located in a John Deere community or with a John Deere employee mentor. Deadlines vary by program (FLL Challenge is earliest, FRC and FTC follow through the fall) — the date shown is the earliest window.
details: Also open to FTC teams in Mexico and Canada, not just the US. Important: register your team with FIRST but do NOT pay the registration fee before applying, or you forfeit eligibility. Applications are reviewed weekly and you'll get an email confirmation once received.

name: Boston Scientific FRC Team Grant
description: For FRC teams within roughly 60 miles of a Boston Scientific site, prioritizing economically disadvantaged schools and communities.
details: Confirm your school/community is within roughly 60 miles of a Boston Scientific site in CA, IN, MA, or MN before applying — proximity is a hard eligibility filter, not just a scoring preference.

name: Boeing Team Grant
description: For FLL, FTC, and FRC teams with a Boeing employee mentor or retiree. US-only for FLL/FTC; open to US and international teams for FRC.
details: Requires a current Boeing employee or retiree connected to the team as a mentor — have their name and employee/retiree status ready when you apply. International FRC teams are eligible even without a US base.

name: NASA FIRST Robotics Competition Grant
description: NASA prioritizes Rookie, New Veteran, and Year-Two FRC teams, covering the first regional or district registration. Deadline is estimated from the prior cycle's pattern — confirm the exact date on NASA's site once the window opens.
details: US teams only — NASA cannot sponsor international teams. Registering for the application site does not register your team with FIRST; you'll need a FIRST team number first, and the portal times out after 120 minutes of inactivity, so save often.

name: Molex FIRST Robotics Sponsorship
description: Ongoing in-kind sponsor providing connector kits built for FIRST applications, plus team and event mentor support.
details: No application deadline — the site lists their SL and CAN connector kits directly; request one through the page or reach out about mentor support if a Molex site is near you.

name: Team REV Sponsorship (FRC)
description: REV Robotics awards a share of a $100,000 sponsorship pool to FRC teams that excel on the field and in community outreach.
amount: Share of $100,000 sponsorship pool + product support
details: Selection favors teams that combine strong on-field performance with real community outreach — be ready to describe both, not just competition results. Teams already sponsored by another FIRST-centric parts vendor are not eligible.

name: Team REV Sponsorship (FTC)
description: REV Robotics awards a share of a $100,000 sponsorship pool to FTC teams that excel on the field and in community outreach.
amount: Share of $100,000 sponsorship pool + product support
details: Same evaluation criteria as the FRC track — field performance plus community outreach. Teams already sponsored by another FIRST-centric parts vendor are not eligible.

name: AndyMark Product Donation Voucher
description: Every registered FRC team can opt into a voucher credited toward checkout in place of a drive base or parts tote.
details: No separate application — every registered FRC team gets a voucher code in their Kit of Parts checkout flow if they opt out of the drive base or tote. Check your team dashboard for the code rather than emailing AndyMark.

name: Siemens Solid Edge FIRST Sponsorship
description: Free Solid Edge CAD software, learning resources, and certification for all FTC and FRC teams, plus funding for qualifying teams.
amount: In-kind: free CAD software + funding for qualifying teams
details: Create a free student/educator account to unlock Solid Edge — no waiting on approval for the software itself. Cash sponsorship for qualifying teams is a separate, more selective track handled through Siemens' FIRST program page.

name: Gene Haas Foundation Student Competition Team Grant
description: Sponsorship for FRC and FTC teams that use CNC machining to build their robot; funds can cover materials, travel, entry fees, and safety gear.
details: Your team must actually use CNC machining in building the robot — describe that in the application. Funds cannot be spent on Haas-manufactured products or Haas Factory Outlet purchases. Applications for this competition season open after May 1. International eligibility: FRC teams outside the US and Canada, and FTC teams in Mexico, can apply directly (May 1 – Sept 15); FTC teams in France, the Netherlands, and the UK should ask their national delivery partner whether GHF funds are available, since those slots are limited.

name: RTX FIRST Grant Program
description: For NAF career academies with an active FIRST team in select RTX geographies; requires an interest form, info session, and a FIRST team number to apply.
amount: Varies; requires active NAF academy + FIRST team number
details: Your school must be a registered NAF academy — this isn't open to any school with a FIRST team. Process is multi-step: submit an interest form, attend an info session, then submit the full application with your FIRST team number. Cycle dates shift year to year, so check naf.org for the current window.

name: DoW STEM Robotics Grant
description: Federal grant covering preseason team or Class Pack costs and FIRST Championship registration; the portal was renamed from DoD STEM to DoW STEM in 2025.
amount: Preseason team/Class Pack costs + Championship registration
details: Federal program — the portal address changed from dodstem.us to dowstem.us after the department's 2025 rename, so double-check you're on the current domain before entering any info. This season's window has closed; the next typically opens in spring.

name: FIRST STEM Equity Community Innovation Grant
description: Pooled fund from corporate partners (3M, Apple, Bosch, Booz Allen Hamilton, Caterpillar, Cognizant, Dow, Qualcomm, RTX, Toyota, Disney and others) supporting community organizations that expand FIRST access for underserved youth.
details: Targeted at community organizations (not individual teams applying solo) working to reach underserved or underrepresented youth — a clear equity/access narrative in your application matters as much as your budget request.

name: West Coast Products (WCP) FRC Team Sponsorship
description: Annual open sponsorship application for FRC teams committed to continuous improvement and community outreach; the 2026 cycle has closed, reopening in summer 2027.
details: WCP looks for teams that show continuous improvement year over year and real community outreach, not just competition wins. This year's window is closed — the 2027 Open Sponsorship Application reopens in summer.

name: Protocase Student Sponsorship
description: No online application — email a brief project description, timeline, and the parts you need, and their team follows up to discuss design and financial need.
amount: Up to $500/year toward custom enclosures & sheet metal parts
details: Email info@protocase.com directly — there's no web form. Include your project timeline, the specific enclosure/sheet-metal parts you need, and your team's financial need; in return you must provide photos and allow Protocase to use your project for marketing.

name: Symbotic Community & STEM Partnerships
description: Warehouse-robotics company headquartered in Wilmington, MA that supports STEM and robotics programs in its home community; there's no public FIRST-specific grant form — teams typically reach out directly about mentorship or sponsorship.
amount: Varies (mentorship, in-kind, or funding by direct arrangement)
details: There is no confirmed public FIRST grant program here — this is a realistic example of a large local employer worth approaching directly, especially for Massachusetts-area teams. Use their partnerships page to find the right community-relations contact rather than a generic info line.

name: National Instruments (NI) FIRST Partnership
description: The roboRIO controller and LabVIEW are included in every FRC kit of parts; NI also considers supplemental team grants, mainly in the Texas community around its headquarters.
amount: roboRIO & LabVIEW included in kit of parts; supplemental grants by request
details: Every FRC team already gets the roboRIO and LabVIEW automatically — no request needed for that part. Supplemental grants beyond the standard kit are handled informally and concentrated around NI's Austin, TX headquarters community.

name: 3M Product & Community Sponsorship
description: 3M supports FIRST globally through product donations (Dual Lock, tape, adhesives) and employee mentors, with regional community grants submitted through My 3Mgives.
amount: In-kind: Dual Lock, tape & adhesive products; occasional regional cash grants
details: Regional cash grants go through 3M's My 3Mgives community engagement portal — submitting a request doesn't guarantee a response, since 3Mgives staff reviews inquiries against current giving priorities. Product donations are handled separately through team mentors.

name: Autodesk Fusion 360 for FIRST
description: Free educational access to Fusion 360 for all FIRST teams, plus the Synthesis robotics simulator Autodesk has sponsored since 2014.
amount: In-kind: free Fusion 360 & Synthesis simulator access
details: Create an Autodesk Education Access account and verify your student/educator status — access is instant once verified, no separate sponsorship review. Renews yearly.

name: PTC Onshape for FIRST
description: Free cloud-native Onshape CAD accounts for all FIRST students and educators, with additional cash sponsorships available to teams with a PTC mentor or customer co-sponsor.
amount: In-kind: free Onshape CAD; cash sponsorship for teams with a PTC mentor
details: Free Onshape education accounts are self-serve at onshape.com/edu — no waiting period. Cash sponsorships are a separate, more selective track that requires a PTC employee mentor or a PTC customer acting as co-sponsor.

name: Studica Robotics Team Discount
description: Discount application for all FIRST teams on robotics kits and parts; subject to review, some exclusions apply.
details: Submit the online discount application with your team number — approval isn't automatic, and some product lines are excluded from the 25% rate, so check the exclusions list on the application page.

name: goBILDA Educational Discount
description: Submit the educational discount request form and goBILDA's team follows up by email with your team's discount code — there's no instant online form completion.
details: There's no instant discount code at checkout — after submitting the form, goBILDA's team manually verifies your team/school status and emails your code, so apply a few days before you need to order.

name: TE Connectivity Request Funding
description: TE has sponsored FIRST teams for 20+ years with TE mentors; local site funding requests go through TE's community responsibility request-funding form.
amount: Varies; local TE site funding request
details: Applicants must be a registered nonprofit, charitable organization, or educational institution able to provide documentation. Funding is prioritized for communities where TE employees actually live and work — a nearby TE site or mentor strengthens your request.

name: Novelis & Ball FIRST Grant
description: A select number of grants for FRC teams building a recycling-themed robot to champion STEM and sustainability in their communities.
amount: Varies; for a recycling-themed robot project
details: Your application needs a specific sustainability/recycling angle tied to your robot or team project — this isn't a general operating grant, and only a limited number are awarded each cycle.

name: Bechtel FIRST Team Sponsorship
description: Sponsors and mentors FRC teams near Bechtel offices and project sites across nine countries; no public per-team form — reach out through Bechtel's community engagement team.
details: Bechtel Group Foundation reviews unsolicited proposals, but you'll need proof of 501(c)(3)/equivalent nonprofit status and be located near a Bechtel office or active project site — the foundation does not fund religious, entertainment, or narrow-interest groups.

name: Caterpillar FIRST Team Sponsorship
description: Sponsors over 200 FIRST teams worldwide, concentrated near Caterpillar sites; there's no standalone application — connect through your regional FIRST Program Delivery Partner or Caterpillar's community engagement team.
details: The Caterpillar Foundation does not accept unsolicited proposals for its major grants — most FIRST team support flows through existing relationships near Caterpillar facilities. You'll need 501(c)(3) status, audited financials, and an IRS Form 990 if you do get invited to apply.

name: General Motors Community Impact Grant
description: General STEM-education community giving program (not FIRST-exclusive) that has funded FIRST robotics centers and teams, such as Kettering University's robotics program.
details: Start with GM's online Eligibility Quiz — you must be a US-based 501(c)(3) in good standing with the IRS. This cycle's window runs through September 30; allow up to eight weeks for review, and no Letter of Inquiry is accepted after the deadline.

name: Micron STEM Opportunity Fund
description: Funds robotics, AI, and semiconductor-aligned STEM programs in Northern Virginia, administered through the Community Foundation for Northern Virginia; the current cycle's application window has closed.
details: Your program must incorporate an AI-related activity, tool, or lesson to qualify — a generic robotics build isn't enough on its own. Priority goes to programs in Boise, ID and Manassas, VA, where Micron has a major presence.

name: Intuitive Foundation FIRST Robotics Grant
description: Awards grants to hundreds of FIRST robotics teams worldwide each year (267 teams in 2024-25), open to teams in Australia, Canada, Israel, Mexico, Türkiye, the UK, and the US.
details: The application portal typically opens in June and closes in August each year — this cycle's window has just closed. Funding is competitive: independent reviewers score every application, and top-scoring teams are funded first as the budget allows.
country: Multiple (AU, CA, IL, MX, TR, UK, US)

name: Actuonix FIRST Robotics Sponsorship
description: Product and cash sponsorship program for FIRST teams, offered up to four times a year; the current round is closed.
details: Runs on a recurring roughly-quarterly cycle rather than one annual deadline — if this round is closed, check back in a few months rather than waiting for next season.

name: Toyota Drive Forward & Rookie Boost FTC Grants
description: Regional Toyota-funded FTC grants for North Texas teams — Drive Forward for existing teams and Rookie Boost for new ones — administered alongside Toyota's broader FIRST robotics STEM giving.
details: Rookie Boost is specifically for brand-new teams and Drive Forward for teams that already have a season under their belt — apply to the one matching your team's history, administered through the North Texas FIRST region rather than nationally.

name: Motorola Solutions Foundation Grant
description: A 20-year FIRST mentor and funder; the annual grants program is a two-stage process (strategic inquiry, then full application) spanning about seven months.
details: Submit a strategic inquiry first — only organizations invited after that stage get to submit a full application. Budget for the long timeline: about seven months from inquiry to a funding decision, so this isn't a fit for urgent, this-season funding needs.

name: FTC SIM Argosy Rookie Team Grant
description: For rookie FTC teams in the US, Mexico, or Canada; cannot be re-granted to a team already receiving other hardship grants.
details: Available to rookie teams in the US, Mexico, and Canada alike. If your team is already receiving another FIRST hardship grant this season, you're not eligible to also receive this one — check for overlap before applying.

name: FIRST Robotics Competition Sustainability Grant
description: One of FIRST HQ's own team grants, aimed at helping established veteran FRC teams sustain their programs.
details: This one is explicitly for teams that already have at least one season of competition history — rookie teams should look at the New Team Grant instead. Check FIRST's team grant hub each season, since it isn't always open.

name: California FIRST Team Grants
description: Aggregates grant opportunities specific to California FLL, FTC, and FRC teams in one hub.
details: This is a directory page, not a single application — it lists several California-specific funders with their own deadlines and criteria, so check back regularly rather than treating it as a one-time apply-and-done resource.

name: FIRST in Texas Team Grants
description: State chapter grant hub distributing corporate and foundation funding to Texas FLL, FTC, and FRC teams.
details: Distributes roughly $700,000 a year to over 350 Texas teams — funding is prioritized by region and program type, with an eye toward teams (including those with students with disabilities) where the money will most expand participation.

name: High Tech Kids Minnesota Team Funding
description: Grants and scholarships for Minnesota FTC, FLL Challenge, and FLL Explore teams.
details: Minnesota-only — this hub lists multiple funding sources including 3M-backed grants, each with its own criteria, so read each listing on the page rather than assuming one blanket application covers all of them.

name: Pennsylvania FIRST Tech Challenge Team Grants
description: State chapter hub listing team grant opportunities available to Pennsylvania FTC teams each season.
details: PA FTC teams have received grants tied to a $200,000 state-level commitment supporting Philadelphia-area teams specifically — check whether your team qualifies for the regional set-asides in addition to the general listings.

name: Montana Robotics Alliance Grants
description: Aggregates grant and funding resources for Montana FLL, FTC, and FRC teams.
details: A resource hub rather than a single grant — worth checking each season since Montana's small-state team count means individual listings can change year to year.

name: FIRST Indiana Robotics Team Grants
description: Includes the Indiana Department of Education Competitive Robotics Grant along with other state-specific team funding.
details: The Indiana Department of Education Competitive Robotics Grant on this page has historically closed in September — treat that one as time-sensitive even though the hub itself is evergreen.

name: KY FIRST Robotics Team Grants
description: Lists Kentucky-specific funding including FJ Foundation grants for new and existing FRC teams, TVA grants for the TVA service region, and Toyota funding for Fayette and Scott county public schools.
details: Three distinct funders live on this one page — FJ Foundation (new + existing FRC), TVA (only within the TVA service region), and Toyota (only Fayette/Scott county public schools). Confirm which one actually matches your team before applying.

name: GeorgiaFIRST Google FTC Team Support Grant
description: Helps under-resourced and traditionally underrepresented middle-school-age FTC teams, including former FLL teams transitioning up to FTC.
details: Covers registration, electronics kit, build kit, driver kit, hand tools, and a partial field set — designed specifically for middle-school teams moving from FLL into FTC, so note that transition explicitly in your application.

name: Hawai'i FIRST Robotics Booz Allen Hamilton Grant
org: Hawai'i FIRST Robotics (funded by Booz Allen Hamilton)
description: Team grant plus a Booz Allen employee mentor; the cycle has historically closed in mid-February, so this date is estimated for the next cycle — confirm on hawaiifirstrobotics.org.
details: Comes paired with an actual Booz Allen employee mentor, not just cash — be ready to describe how your team would use ongoing engineering mentorship, not only the funding.

name: Honda Canada Foundation FIRST Robotics Grant
description: Part of a three-year, $375,000 partnership with FIRST Robotics Canada, funding $2,000 per Canadian high-school FRC team.
details: The online application takes about 30–45 minutes — all funding requests are handled only through this form, so don't email the foundation directly. Open to Canadian high-school FRC teams provincially and at the national championship level.

name: FIRST Robotics Canada National Grants Hub
description: Aggregates national-level Canadian funding including the Lockheed Martin Canada National Gold partnership (over $100,000/season) alongside registration-fee grants.
details: For registration-fee grant inquiries specifically, the page directs teams to contact FIRST Robotics Canada's team support staff directly rather than filling out a public form — email is the actual application channel here.

name: FIRST LEGO League UK Funding Packages
description: Funding packages for UK educational institutions, home education groups, and youth groups across FLL Explore and FLL Challenge.
amount: Varies (covers Team Event Registration or Class Pack)
details: Decide upfront whether you're applying for a Team Event Registration (competing at an event) or a Class Pack (running the programme in-house for up to 30 students) — the funding packages differ. Reviewed on impact, the demographic reached, and plans for continuing beyond one season.

name: FIRST Australia Team Support
description: Central page for one-off donations or ongoing sponsorship of Australian FIRST teams, covering registration, materials, travel, accommodation, and mentors.
details: This page is framed more as 'how to give' than a team-facing application form — if you're a team looking for funding rather than a sponsor looking to give, contact FIRST Australia directly through the site to be connected with available support.

name: FTC India Sponsor-a-Student Program
description: Sponsors a student's share of FTC India Championship registration fees, targeted at talented students from underprivileged backgrounds.
details: This is a per-student sponsorship, not a team-wide grant — you nominate individual students from underprivileged backgrounds who show potential and passion, and each sponsorship covers that one student's championship registration share.

name: Robotique FIRST France Team Funding Support
description: France's national FIRST partner helps FLL, FTC, and FRC teams find regional grants, corporate sponsors, and local-authority subsidies rather than offering one central fund.
amount: Varies (regional subsidies & corporate sponsors, e.g. past 1,500€ Pays de la Loire Region and 2,000€ Haas Foundation grants)
details: There's no single national grant to apply for — regional mentors help teams build a funding plan, recruit local companies as sponsors, and pursue subsidies from regional authorities. Past examples include a 1,500€ grant from the Pays de la Loire Region and a 2,000€ Haas Foundation subsidy for four teams. Note: this national site has occasionally returned server errors to automated checks — if the page doesn't load, try again shortly or search "Robotique FIRST France" directly.

name: BRD FIRST Tech Challenge Romania Program
org: Nație prin Educație (BRD – Groupe Société Générale)
description: Nație prin Educație is FIRST's official Program Delivery Partner in Romania, running FTC Romania with over 10 years of sponsorship from BRD; teams register through the national program rather than applying to BRD directly.
amount: Varies (funds the national program; team-level support arranged locally)
details: There's no separate BRD application form — teams register for the season through Nație prin Educație's national FTC Romania program, which BRD funds at the program level. Reach out to Nație prin Educație directly for team-level funding help.

name: stemOS FTC & FRC Sponsorship Program
description: Brazilian robotics supplier stemOS sponsors a set of FTC and FRC teams each season across Brazil; support goes to specific pre-selected teams rather than an open general application.
amount: Varies (parts, program materials & support for selected teams)
details: The page lists specific teams already receiving sponsorship rather than a public application form — contact stemOS directly (via their site or WhatsApp) about being considered for a future season, and check their 2026/27 FTC and FRC regulations documents for program specifics.

name: FIRST LEGO League Germany, Austria & Switzerland Funding
org: HANDS on TECHNOLOGY e.V. (with Dow, John Deere Foundation, Motorola Solutions Foundation, Novelis, OTIS, Infineon)
description: Regional funding pools for FLL Explore, Challenge, and Future Edition 8+ teams in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, backed by corporate sponsors tied to specific plant regions.
amount: Season materials & participation fees; some sites add mentor support or team T-shirts
details: Only available to teams in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Each sponsor covers a specific region: Dow (Stade, Schkopau, Böhlen sites), John Deere Foundation (Rhine-Neckar region, plus Mühlviertel/Linz jointly with KREISEL Electric), Motorola Solutions Foundation (Germany & Austria, limited slots), Novelis (near Novelis sites), OTIS Holdings, and Infineon (Dresden, capped at two teams). Complete the FIRST LEGO League funding application form and email it in — slots are limited and some sponsors are already fully awarded for the season.

name: ASML FIRST LEGO League Netherlands Sponsorship
description: ASML has sponsored the Dutch FIRST LEGO League national finals since 2021 alongside SMC, Korein, Frencken, and Philips, including funding the ASML Innovation Prize awarded to a competing team each year.
amount: National event sponsorship + ASML Innovation Prize award
details: This is national-event-level sponsorship, not a per-team application — there's no direct funding form for individual teams. Some ASML employees also mentor Dutch FLL teams directly (e.g. Sondervick College in Veldhoven); approaching a local ASML site about mentorship is more realistic than seeking direct funding.

name: General Motors de México FIRST Robotics Support
description: GM de México has backed FIRST Robotics Competition teams in Mexico for 19+ years with funding and engineer mentor hours; support is arranged directly rather than through a public application form.
details: No public application form — GM de México works through existing FIRST México relationships to fund and mentor Mexican FRC teams. Reach out through FIRST México (first.org.mx) or GM's community affairs team to ask about your team's eligibility.

name: FIRST México National Network
description: Mexico's national FIRST organization runs FLL, FTC, and FRC programs and lists partner institutions (including ITAM, Prepatec, Tec Milenio, GM, Peñoles, and Fundación Azteca) that teams can seek support from.
amount: Varies (connects teams to partner institutions & sponsors)
details: This is a resource and partner-network hub rather than a single grant application — with 499+ Mexican teams and 599+ mentors in the network, contact FIRST México directly to be connected with the partner organization most relevant to your team's region and program.

name: FIRST India National Hub
description: India's national FIRST organization runs FLL, FTC, and FRC programs; FTC was introduced in India in 2010 with founding partners PTC and NRB Bearings, and the hub connects teams to current sponsors and support.
details: This is a directory/resource hub rather than a single application — contact FIRST India directly for current sponsor and funding leads for your program and region.

name: Lockheed Martin Canada National Gold Partnership
description: Lockheed Martin joined FIRST Robotics Canada as a National Gold partner for 2025-26, representing over $100,000 in support and connecting its roughly 1,000-person Canadian workforce as team mentors and volunteers.
amount: Share of $100,000+ national partnership; priority for teams with a Lockheed Martin employee mentor
details: This is a national-level partnership rather than a per-team application form — teams with a Lockheed Martin Canada employee mentor or volunteer are best positioned to benefit. Contact FIRST Robotics Canada directly to ask how the partnership applies to your team.

name: FIRST UK Equipment Bursaries & Travel Awards
org: FIRST UK (backed by Arm, Bloomberg, Lockheed Martin, RTX, Qualcomm)
description: FIRST UK provides equipment bursaries and travel awards for FIRST Tech Challenge teams, backed by corporate partners including Arm, Bloomberg, Lockheed Martin, RTX, and Qualcomm.
details: Aimed at teams who would benefit most from support accessing robotics-based, industry-linked skills development — check the financial support page directly for the current application window and criteria.

name: Equinor Sponsorship of the SESI FIRST Tournament
description: Norwegian energy company Equinor began sponsoring SESI's national FIRST Tech Challenge & FIRST LEGO League Challenge tournament in Brazil starting the 2024-25 season, alongside stemOS-supported teams.
amount: Event-level sponsorship (regional/national tournament registration stays free)
details: This is tournament-level sponsorship through SESI (Brazil's official FTC/FLL operator), not a per-team funding form — free regional tournament slots are limited, so register with SESI as soon as registration opens for your region.

name: Michigan Section 99h Robotics Competition Grant
description: State-legislated competitive grant (up to $5.6M statewide) for Michigan districts, intermediate districts, and nonpublic schools running FLL, FTC, or FRC robotics programs.
details: Applicant must be a district, intermediate district, or nonpublic school (not an individual team) with at least one outside sponsor/partner, a submitted budget, and a local cash/in-kind match of at least 25% of the award. FY26 applications closed Feb 9, 2026 — the FY27 cycle is expected on a similar winter timeline; confirm the exact date on MDE's grants page before applying.

name: Wisconsin Robotics League Participation Grant
description: State-funded grant (about $1M statewide per year, established by 2015 Wisconsin Act 280) reimbursing Wisconsin teams up to $6,000 for participating in a 501(c)(3)-sponsored robotics competition.
amount: Up to $6,000 per team (prorated if total requests exceed the statewide pool)
details: Requires matching funds equal to the grant request secured before you apply, and covers students in grades 6-12 (public, charter, private, or home-based). After competing, teams submit form PI-2774 with itemized receipts showing both grant and matching-fund spending. Grant period runs July 1 through June 30 each year.

name: Washington OSPI FIRST Robotics Grant
org: Washington Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction (via FIRST Washington)
description: State-funded grant (about $1.4M statewide in 2023-24) distributed through FIRST Washington to public schools and tribal compact schools running FLL, FTC, or FRC teams for grades 4-12.
amount: Varies by need (statewide pool has fluctuated with the state budget)
details: Register your team with FIRST and get a team number before applying. Funding is state-budget-dependent — Washington's 2025 budget shortfall put continued funding in question, so confirm current-year availability on the FIRST Washington OSPI page before counting on it.

name: Colorado FIRST Rookie & Hardship Grant
description: Grants for Colorado teams starting a rookie FRC season or veteran teams facing genuine financial hardship to continue competing.
details: This is a hardship-based grant, not general operating support — be ready to describe your team's specific financial need. Applications are due before September 1 each year for the following season.

name: Maryland Robotics Grant Program
description: State grant program funding roughly 35 awards of $5,000-$15,000 to Maryland local education agencies, schools, and nonprofits partnered with public schools to start or expand robotics programs.
details: Applicants must be a Local Education Agency (LEA) or a nonprofit partnered with a Maryland public K-12 school — individual teams cannot apply directly and should apply through their school or district. Check the MSDE grants page each year for the current FY cycle's open window.

name: KC STEM Alliance Targeted Grant Making
description: Targeted grants for FTC and FRC teams in the Kansas City metro (Johnson & Wyandotte counties, KS; Cass, Clay, Jackson & Platte counties, MO), prioritizing underserved communities and recent start-up teams.
amount: Varies (past FTC grants averaged $728, ranging $200-$1,000); amount set by review board and funds available
details: Only open to schools/nonprofits in the specific KC-metro counties listed, serving low-income students (at least 21% free/reduced lunch eligible) or underserved groups. FTC applications close Sept 18, FRC applications close Sept 21. Contact bkelley@kcstem.org for application issues; winners are notified within 3 weeks.

name: ORTOP (FIRST Oregon) Team Support Award
description: Oregon's FIRST affiliate raises roughly $1M a year from corporate sponsors, foundations, and donors to reduce financial and systemic barriers for underserved and underrepresented Oregon FLL, FTC, and FRC teams.
details: Schools and nonprofit organizations (not individual students) apply for a team support award. ORTOP supports up to 650 teams and 7,500 students a year across Oregon; applications for the current season open on the team support page.

name: AEP Foundation Robotics Team Grant
description: Utility-funded grants ($250-$6,000 depending on program level) for FIRST robotics teams within AEP's service territory across Ohio, Oklahoma, Indiana, Michigan, Kentucky, Texas, West Virginia, Virginia, Tennessee, Arkansas, and Louisiana.
details: Applications typically open October 1 with a late-January deadline, and awards are announced by mid-March. Only teams within AEP's specific utility service area are eligible — email community@aep.com to confirm your team's district qualifies before applying.

name: Rocky Mountain Power Foundation STEM/Robotics Grant
description: Utility foundation grants (typically $2,000-$5,000) supporting FIRST Robotics teams in Utah, Wyoming, and southeastern Idaho with parts, tools, batteries, and other competition needs.
details: Apply through Rocky Mountain Power Foundation's online grant portal under the Education/STEM funding cycle, which closes March 15 each year. Only teams within Rocky Mountain Power's Utah/Wyoming/southeastern-Idaho service territory are eligible.

name: FIRST Mid-Atlantic Regional Support
description: Regional FIRST Robotics Competition affiliate serving Delaware, New Jersey, and eastern Pennsylvania counties from Harrisburg east, connecting teams to regional sponsors and funding leads.
details: This is a regional program-delivery hub rather than a single grant application — contact FIRST Mid-Atlantic directly for current funding leads specific to your Delaware, New Jersey, or eastern Pennsylvania team.

name: EDF Foundation Robotics Mentorship Program
description: EDF Group's corporate foundation funds robot construction kits, the regional Défi Robotique competition in the Lyon area, and event/travel costs for French FTC teams, plus EDF employee skills-based mentoring.
amount: Covers robot kits, competition organization & travel; students only pay a 250 euro team registration fee
details: Open to students aged 11-18 regardless of academic record — schools just need to provide a workspace for building. EDF covers the kit, event organization, and travel costs, and EDF employees can get involved as mentors through the foundation's skills-sponsorship program. Contact Robotique FIRST France to be connected with an EDF-backed team slot.

name: Otis Poland & Future Minds Foundation FLL Partnership
description: Otis Poland partners with Fundacja Future Minds (the national FIRST LEGO League Poland operator) to fund FLL participation for underserved schools across the country.
amount: Full season sponsorship for selected schools (roughly 10 schools / 70 students per round)
details: Otis funds cohorts of schools through Future Minds Foundation rather than accepting direct team applications — reach out to Future Minds Foundation to ask about current or upcoming Otis-sponsored slots for your school.

name: Rockwell Automation FLL Poland Regional Sponsorship
description: Rockwell Automation increases its sponsorship of FIRST LEGO League Poland's regional tournaments each year, funding more participating teams and providing employee judges and mentors.
amount: Varies (regional tournament sponsorship, growing year over year)
details: This is tournament-level sponsorship funneled through Fundacja Future Minds (the national FLL Poland operator) rather than a per-team application — Rockwell employees also serve as volunteer judges at Polish regional and championship events.

name: FIRST LEGO League Poland ChangeX & Microsoft Mini-Grant
org: Fundacja Future Minds (with ChangeX & Microsoft Datacenter Community Development)
description: A scholarship and mini-grant program that lets local leaders — teachers, parents, community organizers — start a brand-new FIRST LEGO League team anywhere in Poland with a full starter package plus funds for transport and materials.
amount: Full starter kit (Discover/Explore/Challenge level) + mini-grant for transport, materials & branding
details: No prior robotics experience or institutional backing required — just a group of children and a motivated adult leader, especially encouraged from smaller towns and resource-limited schools. Awarded first-come, first-served until each round's funding is used up, so apply as soon as a new round opens.

name: FIRST LEGO League Spain Becas (Iniciación / Continuidad / Impulso)
description: Three-tier scholarship program covering FLL Spain registration fees for teams that are new to the program, returning teams whose prior scholarship ended, or teams facing access barriers like special-needs centers or refugee status.
amount: Beca Impulso covers 100% of registration; Beca Continuidad covers 50%; Beca Iniciación varies by need
details: Beca Iniciación is for first-time teams facing financial barriers; Beca Continuidad is for teams that received a scholarship before and still need support; Beca Impulso (100% of fees) targets teams with specific access difficulties such as special-needs centers, rural schools, or refugee groups — priority also goes to teams that are at least 50% girls. Email FLLSpain@ingeniera.soy to ask which tier fits your team.

name: Bilim Kahramanları Derneği FIRST LEGO League Türkiye
description: Türkiye's national FIRST LEGO League operator since 2004, running the program under the name "Bilim Kahramanları Buluşuyor" across Discover, Explore, and Challenge divisions.
amount: Varies (national program administration; team-level funding arranged through local sponsors)
details: This is Türkiye's official FLL delivery partner rather than a direct grant form — contact the association about regional tournament participation and any current sponsor-backed team slots, alongside the separately-listed Fikret Yüksel Foundation grant for Turkish FRC teams.

name: FIRST Egypt Tech Challenge Program
description: Techno Future Egypt operates FIRST Tech Challenge and other FIRST programs in Egypt, helping students form and register teams and pursue FIRST's college scholarship network.
amount: Varies (team formation support; students may also access $80M+ in FIRST-network college scholarships)
details: No public per-team funding form is listed — teams are expected to fundraise locally with organizational support from Techno Future Egypt. Use the site's "Start a Team" page to begin, and ask Techno Future Egypt directly about any current sponsor-backed slots.

name: FIRST LEGO League Korea (Sangsang / Imagine Association)
description: South Korea's official FIRST LEGO League Program Delivery Organization, running national competitions including the FLL Korea Open Invitational, which drew 50+ teams from 45+ countries in 2026.
amount: Varies (national program administration; team-level funding arranged directly)
details: No public team-funding application is listed online — contact Sangsang/Imagine Association directly (fll.korea@imagine.or.kr) to ask about registration support or sponsor-backed team slots for Korean schools.

name: Enbridge Gas Ontario FIRST Robotics Sponsorship
description: Enbridge Gas has backed FIRST Robotics Canada with recurring $70,000 Platinum-level sponsorships since 2013, most recently in March 2026, funding direct support to about ten Ontario student robotics teams per round.
amount: $70,000 CAD shared across roughly 10 Ontario teams per sponsorship round
details: Funding is distributed to Ontario teams through FIRST Robotics Canada rather than via a direct team application — contact FIRST Robotics Canada to ask whether the current Enbridge round is open and how Ontario teams are selected.

name: FIRST Robotics BC Team Grants (First West & Y.P. Heung Foundations)
org: FIRST Robotics BC (with First West Foundation & Y.P. Heung Foundation)
description: British Columbia's FIRST Robotics hub lists province-specific grants — including First West Foundation and Y.P. Heung Foundation funding open to any team status — alongside pass-through national and US grants relevant to BC teams.
amount: Varies by grant; most are open to teams of any status
details: This page aggregates several BC-specific and pass-through grants with their own windows and criteria (First West Foundation, Y.P. Heung Foundation, plus BC-relevant national grants) — check back each season since availability windows shift, and contact FIRST Robotics BC directly for the current application details.

name: FTC Hardship Grant
description: A one-time FIRST-run grant covering FIRST Tech Challenge season registration costs for teams facing financial hardship in the US, Mexico, or Canada.
details: This is distinct from the Rookie Grant — it's aimed at any team (rookie or veteran) demonstrating genuine financial hardship, not just new teams. Funds can only be applied toward FTC season registration, not general team expenses.

name: FIRST Robotics Competition New Team Grant
description: FIRST's own grant for brand-new and new-veteran FRC teams, covering season registration with a follow-up grant the next year.
details: Register your team and get a team number before applying — do not pay your registration fee first, since the grant is meant to be applied directly at storefront checkout. Funds can be used for registration, event fees, or other FIRST Storefront purchases.

name: FIRST Tech Challenge Rookie Team Grant
description: FIRST's own grant specifically for brand-new FTC teams, covering season registration and products, submitted through FIRST's Submittable portal.
details: Distinct from the Hardship Grant — this one is rookie-only and doesn't require demonstrating financial hardship. Funding is limited and awarded until each season's budget is exhausted, so apply as early as your rookie season allows.

name: FIRST Class Pack Rookie Team Grant
description: FIRST's own grant covering the Class Pack option for new FLL/FTC classroom groups, submitted through FIRST's Submittable portal.
details: For groups running the in-classroom Class Pack format rather than competing at an event — check FIRST's Team Grant Opportunities hub each season for the current window and funding amount.

name: Bishop-Wisecarver FIRST Sponsorship
description: A Diamond-level FIRST supplier since 2007, sponsoring select FRC and VEX teams with funding, product donations, and a factory tour, with a focus on California's Contra Costa County area.
amount: Varies; includes a factory tour of their manufacturing facility
details: Priority goes to local high schools near their California facility, though they've expanded to some out-of-state teams. Email mteam@bwc.com or call (925) 439-8272 with questions, and check their giving-guidelines application form before applying. Linear motion parts are also available in-kind through AndyMark FIRST Choice team credits.

name: ServoCity FIRST Team Discount
description: A 25% discount on nearly all ServoCity products for FIRST teams, activated through an online discount application.
details: Submit the discount application online — most approvals land within one business day by email. Orders placed before your discount is activated are not refunded retroactively, so apply before you start buying parts for the season.

name: REV Robotics FTC Team Discount
description: A 15% discount on select REV Robotics items for every registered FTC team, separate from REV's larger FRC/FTC sponsorship pool.
details: Find your team's unique voucher code in the FIRST Dashboard (visible to the primary/secondary coach), or fill out REV's Team Registration Form to have the code emailed directly. Only applies to specific listed products and can't be applied retroactively to past orders.

name: Swerve Drive Specialties FRC Team Voucher
description: A $25 one-time voucher donated to every registered FRC team, redeemable on Swerve Drive Specialties' site.
details: Find your team's voucher code in the FIRST Dashboard (Lead Mentor 1 or 2 access). Valid only for online purchases at swervedrivespecialties.com, one-time use, and any unused balance is forfeited — check the expiration date each season, since it resets annually.

name: FedEx Rookie Grant Program & In-Kind Shipping
description: FedEx has supported FIRST since 2002, sponsoring a multi-year Rookie Grant Program for new FRC teams and providing in-kind shipping of robots and kits to and from competitions.
amount: Personalized sponsorship & mentoring for selected rookie teams; in-kind competition shipping
details: The Rookie Grant Program selects new teams to track over a multi-year period rather than running an open rolling application — reach out through FIRST's sponsor channels to ask about current-cycle availability. The in-kind shipping support is arranged at the event/regional level, not per-team.

name: L3Harris Foundation Robotics Grants
description: L3Harris Foundation funds robotics teams (including FIRST) at the elementary, middle, and high school level, awarding roughly $120,000 across teams in a recent season plus employee volunteer mentoring.
amount: Varies (part of ~$120,000 in recent-season robotics grants)
details: There's no single public application form — L3Harris Foundation grants are often tied to employee/community relationships near L3Harris sites. Reach out through L3Harris's community affairs or foundation contacts to ask about your team's eligibility, and check for an employee mentor connection first.

name: FIRST LEGO League Ireland Funding Packages
org: FLL Ireland (funded by Taighde Éireann - Research Ireland, Science Foundation Ireland Discover Program & IET sponsors)
description: Funding packages for schools, colleges, home school groups, and youth groups in the Republic of Ireland running FLL Explore, Challenge, or Future Edition teams, assessed case-by-case with priority for under-resourced groups.
amount: Varies (covers registration & program materials; assessed case-by-case)
details: Assessment weighs social mobility, free-school-meal eligibility, special educational needs, English-language-learner status, DEIS school designation, and expected community impact. Successful applicants must complete agreements/consent forms, attend training, give ongoing feedback, and either run in-house events or attend designated tournaments. 2026-27 funding applications were listed as opening soon at time of writing — check the page for the current window (allow up to five weeks for a decision after the closing date).

name: FIRST South Africa Explore & Challenge Grants
description: Class Pack grants providing FLL Explore and Challenge kits to South African schools and community centers, with a focus on under-served communities, subject to available sponsorship funding.
amount: Class Pack kits (2-3 team kits per grant); no cash amount
details: Explore grants are limited to learners aged 6-10 (max 6 per team); a separate Challenge grant page covers older students. FIRST South Africa is upfront that grant availability depends entirely on the sponsorship funding they can secure — at time of writing, the Explore grants page states no grants are currently available. Coaches who do receive equipment must submit session reports and return non-consumable equipment if the team doesn't continue. Email explore@firstsa.org to ask about the next funding round.

name: FIRST Robotics Canada FTC First-Year Team Grant
description: A national grant application specifically for Canadian teams in their first year of FIRST Tech Challenge, distinct from FIRST Robotics Canada's general national grants hub.
details: Specifically for teams in their first FTC season in Canada, separate from the general FIRST Robotics Canada grants hub already listed. This page returns a 403 to some automated fetch tools (consistent with other firstroboticscanada.org pages, likely bot-protection rather than a dead page) — confirmed live via search indexing with a matching title. Check directly on firstroboticscanada.org if the link doesn't load in your browser.

name: Alabama AMSTI Robotics Grant
description: State-funded grant for Alabama public K-12 schools to purchase robotics equipment and supplies, with up to $100,000 set aside specifically for elementary robotics programs.
details: Any Alabama public school serving K-12 students can apply; districts may submit identical applications for multiple schools. Funds cover robotics equipment and supplies only, not general computing devices. The application requires four signers (project manager, technology coordinator, CFO, superintendent) via DocuSign and must be completed in one sitting — start early. Deadline is September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM; recipients announced in early 2027.

name: New Hampshire Robotics Education Development Program Grant
description: Competitive state grant for New Hampshire public and public charter schools to establish new robotics teams and fund participation in competitive events like FIRST.
details: Requires an established partnership with at least one sponsor and a plan to participate in at least one competitive event. Proposals are scored by independent peer reviewers; check the NH DOE STEM education office page for the current grant cycle's request-for-applications and deadline, since this runs on a periodic two-year cycle rather than a fixed annual date.

name: Nevada Rural Robotics Partnership (Tesla / OSIT / Pennington Foundation)
org: FIRST Nevada (funded by Tesla, Nevada OSIT & William N. Pennington Foundation)
description: A state-backed partnership that channeled a $315,550 Tesla grant plus a $100,350 William N. Pennington Foundation grant through FIRST Nevada to grow robotics education, with a focus on rural Nevada schools.
amount: Varies (funded via a $315,550 Tesla grant + $100,350 Pennington Foundation grant to FIRST Nevada)
details: Funding flows through FIRST Nevada and Nevada's Office of Science, Innovation and Technology (OSIT) rather than a direct per-team application — contact FIRST Nevada to ask about current program support, with priority historically given to rural Nevada schools starting new robotics programs.

name: Illinois FTC Matching Funds & Hardship Grants
description: Illinois's FIRST program delivery partner offers a Matching Funds Grant (with a separate track for Chicago Public Schools teams) and a Headquarters Hardship Grant for FTC teams statewide.
amount: Varies (matching-funds model; separate hardship track for teams in genuine need)
details: Chicago Public Schools teams use a separate version of the Matching Funds Grant application from the general Illinois application. The Hardship Grant is aimed at teams facing financial difficulty rather than requiring matching funds. FIRST Illinois Robotics also separately lists FLL Challenge grants for new and returning teams on a need basis.

name: FIRST in Upper Midwest Equity & Inclusion Grants
description: Regional FIRST Robotics Competition affiliate for Minnesota, North Dakota, and South Dakota running recurring Equity and Inclusion Grant rounds plus general team launch/growth funding, and acting as fiscal host for other funders' grants.
details: Funding specifically targets underrepresented communities gaining access to FRC. Grant rounds have run periodically (most recently referenced Fall 2023) rather than on one fixed annual date — check the FIRST in Upper Midwest site for the current round's open window, especially if your team is in North Dakota or South Dakota where this is the primary regional funding source.

name: Optimum (Altice USA) FIRST Robotics Team Sponsorship
description: Optimum sponsors 70+ FIRST Robotics Competition teams across its NY/NJ/NC/TX footprint (FIRST Long Island, Mid-Atlantic, North Carolina, Texas, NYC, and Hudson Valley regions), plus Innovator Awards for winning teams.
amount: Team-level sponsorship; Innovator Awards pay $2,000 (winner), $1,500 (runner-up), $500 (honorable mention)
details: This is regional sponsorship tied to Optimum's service footprint rather than an open national application — teams in the Long Island, Mid-Atlantic, North Carolina, Texas, NYC, or Hudson Valley FIRST regions are the ones eligible for direct sponsorship; the Innovator Awards are a separate seasonal competition recognizing community engagement, technology, inspiration, diversity, and sustainability.

name: Digi-Key Electronics FIRST Robotics Support
description: Diamond-level FIRST Robotics Competition supporter since 2012, supplying every team's Kit of Parts with a $50 voucher toward components on digikey.com, plus regional event sponsorship.
amount: $50 voucher (included automatically in the FRC Kit of Parts) + regional event sponsorship
details: No separate application — the $50 voucher ships with every team's official Kit of Parts each season. Digi-Key also sponsors the Great Northern Regional (Grand Forks, ND) directly and provides employee judges and mentors at events near its Minnesota headquarters.

name: Mouser Electronics FIRST Championship & Tarrant County Team Grants
description: Registration sponsor of the FIRST Robotics Championship since 2014, and a direct funder of FRC team grants for high schools in Tarrant County, Texas, near its Mansfield headquarters.
amount: Varies (Tarrant County team grants); Championship-level sponsorship benefits all competing teams indirectly
details: The Tarrant County team grants aren't a public online application — reach out to Mouser's community outreach team directly if your high school team is in that area. The Championship registration sponsorship isn't a per-team funding source, but it's part of why FIRST can keep Championship costs down for all qualifying teams.
